raw_response:
I’m 65 now, so I don’t like taking big risks. What I do is mostly what has worked on my land, and I watch what the other people in the village are doing. This year I’ll still keep most of my land in wheat-maize, because that gives steady grain and doesn’t leave the land idle. I’ll keep some cotton because I know how to manage it and it brings cash if the price is decent, and I’ll keep a small garlic plot because it sells earlier and helps with household cash. Fertilizer is expensive, water costs money, so I won’t chase the highest yield. I’d rather use enough to keep the crop from looking weak, then add a bit more only if I see it needs it. On the wheat already in the field, I’ll give it one more water and topdressing if the stand stays good. After wheat harvest I’ll rush in maize on the same land, no fancy tillage, just quick turnover. Cotton I’ll keep a bit lighter on fertilizer than some young farmers do, because too much spending at my age is not safe. Garlic needs more hand work, but my family can still handle a small area.
